OccurrenceCleaner

quality flags for occurrence records, at any scale

OccurrenceCleaner is an extension of CoordinateCleaner (Zizka et al. 2019) tailored to large-scale occurrence data. It flags common problems in species occurrence records. These include coordinates at country centroids, capitals or biodiversity institutions; zero or equal coordinates; records at sea or in the wrong country; and duplicates. It also reads three GBIF fields: the quality warnings GBIF attaches to a record during processing (such as invalid or rounded coordinates, a fuzzy taxon match or an unlikely date), the basis of record (fossil or living specimens), and the establishment means (introduced or cultivated individuals).

Each test stores its result as one bit per record. No records are removed: users decide afterwards which flags to use for filtering.

The tests and default buffers follow CoordinateCleaner, and the test suite checks that both packages return the same flags. The difference is speed and scale: OccurrenceCleaner flags data frames containing a few million records in seconds and processes GBIF snapshots containing billions of records by reading Parquet files in chunks.

library(OccurrenceCleaner)

x <- data.frame(species = c("Quercus robur", "Quercus robur", "Fagus sylvatica"),
                decimalLongitude = c(12.58, 0, 16.37),
                decimalLatitude = c(55.67, 0, 48.21))
flag_occurrences(x)

The result is x with an integer flags column and one logical flag_<test> column per test. The first record is within 1 km of the GBIF headquarters and 10 km of Copenhagen, the second is a zero coordinate at sea, the third is in Vienna, a capital.

Several rules from one pass

A rule is a set of tests. has_flag() marks the records a rule removes, and tally_flags() compares several rules on the same flags:

f <- flag_occurrences(x, tests = c("val", "zero", "equ", "cap", "cen", "inst", "gbif", "sea"))

strict <- has_flag(f$flags, c("zero", "equ", "cap", "cen", "inst", "gbif", "sea"))
mild   <- has_flag(f$flags, c("zero", "equ", "gbif"))

tally_flags(f, by = "species",
            rules = list(strict = c("zero", "equ", "cap", "cen", "inst", "gbif", "sea"),
                         mild = c("zero", "equ", "gbif")))

tally_flags() gives, per group, the number of records each test flags and the number each rule removes and keeps. Year and coordinate uncertainty stay raw columns and are cut at tally time with bins.

A whole GBIF snapshot

The same verb streams an on-disk table through vectra: a directory of Parquet parts (a GBIF snapshot), a .vtr file, a delimited file or any vectra_node. Each input file is one resumable unit, and the flags are written as .vtr parts next to the columns you keep for grouping:

f <- flag_occurrences("gbif_snapshot/occurrence.parquet",
                      tests = c(default_tests(), "coun", "rounded", "fossil"),
                      out = "flags",
                      keep = c("kingdom", "year", "coordinateuncertaintyinmeters"))

tally_flags(f, by = "kingdom",
            bins = list(year = c(1950, 1970, 1990, 2000),
                        coordinateuncertaintyinmeters = c(10, 100, 1000)),
            rules = list(cc = c("zero", "equ", "cap", "cen", "inst", "gbif", "sea")))

Rerunning the same call after an interruption skips the input files already finished.

What’s in the box

  • flag_occurrences(): the one flagging verb. Data frame in, data frame out; path or vectra_node in, flag parts on disk out.
  • tally_flags(): flags to a loss table by any grouping columns, with bins and named rules.
  • has_flag(), flag_mask(): a rule as a bit mask over the flag word.
  • flag_tests(): the versioned flag layout: bit, test, definition, source, CoordinateCleaner equivalent.
  • default_tests(): the CoordinateCleaner-equivalent tests that need only coordinates and a species name.
  • occ_columns(): which columns hold which field; Darwin Core defaults, case-insensitive.
  • reference_info(), download_reference(): the pinned gazetteers (source, version, SHA-256) and the on-demand 1:10m land layer.
  • read_flagged(), flagged_table(): open on-disk flag output as a vectra table.

Tests

test definition source
val coordinate missing or out of range cc_val
zero zero longitude or latitude, or within 0.5 degrees of (0, 0) cc_zero
equ absolute longitude equals absolute latitude cc_equ
cap within 10 km of a capital cc_cap
cen within 1 km of a country or province centroid cc_cen
inst within 100 m of a biodiversity institution cc_inst
gbif within 1 km of the GBIF headquarters cc_gbif
sea outside the land polygons (Natural Earth, scale 110, 50 or 10) cc_sea
urb inside an urban area cc_urb
coun outside the country given by the record’s country code cc_coun
dupl same coordinates and species as an earlier record cc_dupl
issue_geo, issue_tax, issue_date, rounded GBIF quality warnings (issue field) on coordinates, taxon match, date, rounding addition
fossil, living basis of record addition
introduced, managed establishment means addition

Proximity tests are closed balls in WGS84 geodesic distance, found with a kd-tree on the unit sphere and decided with the Vincenty inverse formula. Polygon tests are planar point-in-polygon against pinned Natural Earth layers through a grid index that resolves boundary cells exactly. The gazetteers are rebuilt from the original public sources (Natural Earth, public domain; GBIF GRSciColl for institutions); reference = "CoordinateCleaner" reads that package’s own tables instead and reproduces its flags. The documented differences, each enforced by a test, are in ?flag_occurrences.

Installation 

# install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("gcol33/OccurrenceCleaner")

Needs a C++ compiler (Rtools on Windows).

License

MIT. CoordinateCleaner (GPL-3) is a suggested package used by the equivalence tests and by reference = "CoordinateCleaner"; none of its code or data is bundled.
